title: Bounding single-copy information causality violations
abstract: Information causality is a physical principle that constrains bipartite post-quantum nonlocal correlations from information-theoretic assumptions. A direct characterization of the correlations satisfying it, however, remains difficult because the defining entropic condition must hold for all admissible protocols in the corresponding task. Here, we formulate the single-copy information causality problem as an optimization over all protocol parameters and simplify it by proving a deterministic reduction. We then show that generic adaptive multi-copy protocols can be represented as single-copy protocols applied to an effective behavior obtained by local wirings. As a consequence, for families of correlations closed under wirings, excluding single-copy violations suffices to exclude all finite-copy adaptive-protocol violations. We formulate the resulting membership and set-inclusion problems as optimization problems and discuss possible semidefinite programming relaxations. As an application, we study expansions of the information causality functional around zero-capacity channels, generalizing a method recently employed by Gachechiladze and Miklin to derive the Tsirelson--Landau--Masanes boundary from information causality. For expansions centered on channels whose output distribution has full support, imposing the second-order constraints for all single-copy protocols characterizes exactly the set of macroscopic locality in the CHSH scenario. Expanding instead around appropriate constant-output channels with perturbations that change the channel support, we show that every single-copy IC violation can be witnessed already at first order with a channel of arbitrarily small capacity.
summary: This paper develops a systematic method to analyze Information Causality (IC) violations by reducing complex multi-copy protocols to single-copy constraints. The authors prove that for many systems, bounding single-copy violations is sufficient to bound all adaptive violations. They derive concrete necessary and sufficient conditions for the CHSH inequality using second-order expansions, significantly advancing the understanding of quantum nonlocality bounds.
main_problem: The paper aims to characterize the constraints imposed by Information Causality (IC) on bipartite post-quantum nonlocal correlations, particularly by bounding single-copy violations.
main_result: Excluding single-copy IC violations is sufficient to exclude all finite-copy adaptive-protocol violations for certain correlation families, and the necessary condition for the CHSH scenario is derived as a simple inequality involving square roots.
method: The authors use optimization techniques, deterministic reductions (Lemmas 1 and 3), and second-order Taylor expansions of the IC functional to simplify the complex entropic constraints.
model_or_system: The study uses an assisted Random Access Coding (RAC) task framework to model the correlations, involving shared probability distributions $P$ and protocols $\pi$. The analysis extends to generalized database entries and the CHSH scenario.
key_observables: The IC deficit ($\Delta_1$ or $\Delta_c$), the quadratic form $\Phi_2$ in the CHSH case, and the derived inequality $|\Theta| \le \sqrt{R} + \sqrt{S}$.
important_parameters: The number of copies ($c$), the capacity of the underlying channel, and the perturbation parameter $\epsilon$ used in expansions.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the deterministic reduction of adaptive protocols to single-copy ones, and the second-order expansions are only valid for small perturbations $\epsilon$.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the notation for the random access coding task defining IC. Figure 2 shows the structure of a single-copy protocol for information causality.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the single-copy IC problem via optimization, proves a deterministic reduction connecting multi-copy to single-copy protocols, then analyzes the convexity of the violation, and finally applies second-order expansions to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for the CHSH scenario.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of information causality constraints, especially the reduction from multi-copy to single-copy bounds, provides powerful new tools for bounding quantum correlations, which is fundamental to quantum information theory.
